## Journal

### 2026-08-11

- [The extraction pass met real conversations before it exists](2026-08-11-first-extraction-dry-run.md) — A v0 extraction prompt run against last week's real quantum-conference turns: both models scored 100% precision, but the flash model extracted zero domain facts while the 70B got the panel roster and three strategic insights — model choice dominated prompt design, and both missed the same disguised preference.
- [M0: the dumbest possible brain, live on the wire](2026-08-11-m0-the-wire.md) — Service on its DMZ address, episodic scratch in Postgres, a deliberately trivial recall, and a stdlib-only Hermes provider shim — capture→store→cross-session-recall proven from both DMZ and LAN vantages in one afternoon.
- [The address that answered twice](2026-08-11-the-address-that-answered-twice.md) — A routine key test found every kaiju inference lane dark: two containers on two hosts both claiming 10.0.13.2, and a dual-homed container whose replies escaped un-NAT'd — the gateway had been silently failing over to cloud for its 'local-first' models.
- [The flash tier finds a home, and PCIe forgives the MoE](2026-08-11-the-flash-tier-finds-a-home.md) — A same-day port of the GB10 model orchestrator to the 4x L4 fleet, gated by measurement: Lightning BF16 TP4 hit 113.8 tok/s at 0.07s TTFT over PCIe — triple the acceptance bar, double its own GB10 number — freeing the GB10's KV budget for the agent's main model.
- [The handoff survives contact with the source — mostly](2026-08-11-the-handoff-survives-contact.md) — Read-before-port verification of all three source systems: the crown jewel is real and portable, but 'hybrid retrieval', 'decay', and 'weekly consolidation' turned out to be plans the docs remembered as facts.
- [The retired system that kept taking notes](2026-08-11-the-retired-system-that-kept-taking-notes.md) — The predecessor memory system, retired months ago on paper, turned out to be live wiring: still MCP-served by a bare python process, still written to four days ago, holding 502 memories — embedded, by luck or lineage, with gyrus's exact model and dimension.
- [Two decisions before code, and a false dichotomy](2026-08-11-two-decisions-before-code.md) — Run-location and embeddings were gated as 'shape the schema and compose' — one was settled by a firewall direction, the other dissolved once we noticed the gateway's 'metered' path and the 'local' path were the same GPUs.
### 2026-08-12

- [Five ways a memory system silently forgets](2026-08-12-m1-the-memory-remembers.md) — M1 shipped — extraction, hybrid retrieval, and a backfill of five months of real conversation — and every bug found at scale was a silent one: memories that were never stored, never matched, or never surfaced, with no error anywhere.
### 2026-08-13

- [A migration the memory didn't notice](2026-08-13-a-migration-the-memory-didnt-notice.md) — Pip moved host, hypervisor, and network zone — from a Proxmox VM on the LAN to a libvirt VM in the DMZ — and gyrus, its memory, needed zero changes, because the service boundary was drawn so the client could be relocated without the service ever knowing.
- [The senses, and letting usage decide what's worth keeping deeply](2026-08-13-thalamus-and-earned-depth.md) — Two architecture decisions in one session: ingestion becomes its own service (thalamus) feeding gyrus a thin contract, and retention depth is gated on earned demand — cheap-ingest everything, deep-store in RAGFlow only what usage proves worth keeping.
- [The blind lane opens](2026-08-13-the-blind-lane-opens.md) — thalamus — the ingestion service — went live and fed gyrus the arXiv lane Ken was blind to: it scanned 100 fresh papers, and gyrus's relevance gate kept exactly the ten in his lane (QAOA, quantum networking, error correction) and extracted them into the knowledge tier, firehose economics solved by the gate rather than by manual triage.
- [The crown jewel turns, once, on real data](2026-08-13-the-crown-jewel-turns.md) — M3's mechanism ran end to end on a real turn — a recalled procedural memory, followed, met failing tools, and the credit engine moved its confidence — proving the falsifiable loop works; then a guard the first cut lacked stopped one noisy turn from trusting that signal too far.
- [The dream pass meets real data, and mostly earns its name](2026-08-13-the-dream-pass-meets-real-data.md) — The distinctive contribution — outcome-driven consolidation — ran for the first time on 2,700 real memories and correctly sorted worth-keeping above noise; but it did so on proxy signals, because the crown-jewel outcome signal still doesn't exist until M3.
- [The tier that was almost deleted](2026-08-13-the-tier-that-was-almost-deleted.md) — The 709 memories the review flagged as noise-to-scope-out turned out to be a first-class tier once we saw them right — curated world-knowledge, not clutter — so M4 reclassified them into a knowledge tier with its own evaluator and a surface to browse them, rather than deleting them.
- [When the plan outran the proof](2026-08-13-when-the-plan-outran-the-proof.md) — In a single session gyrus grew from 'port a memory engine' into a multi-service knowledge platform with three new ADRs and a second project — and a deliberate scope review caught that the distinctive contribution had never run and the falsifiable claim had no data, so we stopped adding and went back to prove the core.
### 2026-08-14

- [The loudest week is not the truest](2026-08-14-the-loudest-week-is-not-the-truest.md) — Ranking a user's interests by raw memory count measured how noisy each week was, not what mattered — breadth (distinct sessions) told the truth, and the real fix was a new source, not a better query.
### 2026-08-15

- [The backlog that could not drain](2026-08-15-the-backlog-that-could-not-drain.md) — 465 turns sat unextracted for three days because the one component that would have retried them had been told to ignore them — and the tool written to drain them nearly erased them instead, because a dead gateway and an empty conversation returned the same value.
- [The cleanup that compounded](2026-08-15-the-cleanup-that-compounded.md) — Executing the audit's repairs in dependency order paid a bonus: re-tiering 1,031 world-knowledge rows turned invisible cross-tier duplicates into foldable same-tier pairs, so the 0.93 merge sweep found 256 merges where the scan had measured 187 — and the store ended the day at 10,966 with every model reference now a shape.
- [The epidemic that didn't replicate](2026-08-15-the-epidemic-that-did-not-replicate.md) — The brief's '15% of the store is duplicates' shrank to 1.5% under a full-store exact scan; 95% of real pairs predate the ivfflat fix, and the embed-outage dedupe skip is real but accounts for ~10 pairs — the scary number was the instrument again.
- [The newsletter that corroborated itself](2026-08-15-the-newsletter-that-corroborated-itself.md) — Pre-commit review of the first full-corpus consolidation caught a legal footer at 29x corroboration — one newsletter restating itself every issue — which forced corroboration to learn the difference between repetition and independence, and the tier firewall had already contained the damage before anyone noticed.
- [The pipeline that was already alive](2026-08-15-the-pipeline-that-was-already-alive.md) — The email lane's plan assumed a dead pipeline needing replacement; twenty minutes of inspection found a live one needing only a forwarding address — the architecture decision inverted from 'build a fetcher' to 'add one thin hop', and the credentials never had to move.
- [What the store is actually worth](2026-08-15-what-the-store-is-actually-worth.md) — First-ever grading of the memories themselves (153-row stratified sample): ~41% of the store is keep-grade, ~45% is noise, ~14% is filed under the wrong evaluator — and the noise is mostly scoping and time, not extraction.

## Gotchas

- [A dual-homed container silently breaks its own published ports](gotchas/dual-homed-container-breaks-dnat.md) — Give a container both a published port and its own macvlan leg on the same subnet as its clients, and DNAT'd connections hang forever: replies exit the macvlan leg and bypass the host's conntrack un-NAT.
- [Returning [] when inference is unreachable lets a batch job erase its own backlog](gotchas/empty-extraction-on-dead-gateway-consumes-backlog.md) — An extraction client that swallowed all failures into an empty result made 'the model found nothing worth keeping' indistinguishable from 'no model answered' — so a batch route stamped its work items complete, on time, having learned nothing.
- [Driving a long model-bound batch over synchronous HTTP orphans work under load](gotchas/http-driven-model-batch-orphans-work.md) — A one-request-per-batch ingest loop looked like it was failing (every curl returned empty) while the server quietly finished each batch anyway — the client timeout was shorter than a batch of model calls, so work committed but the client never saw it, causing wasteful re-extraction and a false failure signal.
- [Supabase's postgres user can't CREATE DATABASE OWNER x until it's granted x](gotchas/supabase-create-database-owner.md) — On Supabase images the admin `postgres` role is not a superuser, so `CREATE DATABASE name OWNER role` fails with 'must be member of role' — GRANT the role to postgres first.
